speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I know that many Singaporeans are concerned about what the ongoing Hyflux restructuring means for our water supply.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Public Utilities Board's (PUB's) priority has been and will always be to ensure Singapore's water security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over many decades, we have diversified our water sources and built up our four national taps.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NEWater and desalinated water are integral to our water security, as they are weather-resilient and can supply water even during dry spells.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As part of our plan to build up our desalination and NEWater capacities for our water security, the Government has partnered the private sector to design, build, own and operate (DBOO) some of our desalination and NEWater plants.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, we have five NEWater plants and three desalination plants.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Out of these, three of the NEWater plants and two of the desalination plants, including Tuaspring, are based on a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The remaining three plants, as well as all our other water supply assets, are owned and operated by PUB.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The PPP model has been useful in allowing us to tap on private sector innovations and cost efficiencies to deliver water services more effectively.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To ensure that water security is never compromised, PUB has put in safeguards as part of the PPP contracts.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Even though PUB does not interfere with the business decisions made by the concession companies, PUB monitors the performance of the plants under the PPP model to ensure that the concession companies can meet their contractual obligations to PUB.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Where there are issues, PUB will require the concession companies to rectify them, failing which, PUB may exercise its rights to terminate the PPP contracts and take control of the plants.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We do not exercise these termination rights lightly but will not hesitate to do so when it becomes necessary to safeguard our water security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As PUB continues to operate its own desalination and NEWater plants, PUB has the operational capabilities, experience and manpower to take over and operate the private plants, should the need arise.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hyflux is currently involved in two PPP projects with PUB: the SingSpring Desalination Plant (SSDP) and the Tuaspring Integrated Water and Power Project (TIWPP).

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: SSDP is owned by SingSpring Trust, which is majority owned by Keppel Infrastructure Trust, with Hyflux owning a minority stake.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The SSDP is not affected by Hyflux's debt and business reorganisation nor is it subject to the moratorium that has been imposed by the Court.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As for TIWPP, it is owned by Tuaspring Pte Ltd (TPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hyflux.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In 2010, PUB called an open tender for a 70 million gallons per day desalination plant to be completed by 2013.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In its tender bid, Hyflux proposed a different business model, one of an integrated desalination and power plant.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hyflux made a business decision to build the power plant that has a capacity significantly more than what the desalination plant needed, with the intention of selling excess power to the national power grid.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hyflux’s bid met PUB’s requirements for constructing and operating a desalination plant and was the most competitive bid among the submissions.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: PUB also took into account Hyflux's expertise and track record.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Thus, PUB awarded the tender to Hyflux in 2011.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As with other such PPP projects, PUB built in safeguards in the Water Purchase Agreement (WPA) signed with TPL.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Since 2017, TPL has been experiencing difficulties fulfilling its contractual obligations under the WPA.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These include a failure to keep the plant reliably operational as required.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More recently, it has also failed to produce financial evidence to demonstrate its ability to keep the plant running for the next six months.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: PUB gave time to TPL to try to sort out its problems, but PUB’s concerns have been growing over time.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: If they failed to do so, PUB would terminate the WPA and take over the desalination plant.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is to ensure that a critical asset remains in safe hands and avoids uncertainty over the operations of the desalination plant.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ultimately, PUB’s actions are based on our overriding objective of ensuring Singapore's water security and that water continues to be reliably produced at the plant to meet the needs of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The purchase price for the desalination plant will be determined by an independent valuer in accordance with the WPA.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: TPL itself has stated that there is a high likelihood for this.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The desalination plant has been and will likely continue to lose money for the next few years.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, PUB would have to incur costs to make good the plant and ensure that it operates reliably for its remaining lifespan.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: However, given TPL's current financial position, PUB is unlikely to recover the compensation sum from TPL.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: PUB’s actions do not weaken either TPL or Hyflux, and do not disadvantage those who have invested in Hyflux.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It positively impacts Hyflux's value and hence the value of the Hyflux shares being offered.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In fact, TPL provides an example of how these safeguards are robust and have served their purpose.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That said, we are always studying ways to strengthen the safeguards and enhance our operations and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will never allow Singapore's national or water security to be compromised.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The first is, the Minister has said that the PPP model still works.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Given that these are critical water assets and having seen what has happened and the assurance from the Minister that the Ministry is looking further into the safeguards that are currently provided, I would like to ask the Minister which are these areas that we think need to be further improved on.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The fact of the matter is that it did occur here and this is an area which we know we cannot take chances on.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My second supplementary question: we would all have residents who are also investors in Hyflux.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The current actions by PUB and the Government, the question that will be asked would be, "Should we bail out Hyflux and, in the process, help all residents and investors, many of whom are Singaporeans?"

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But there are two important areas that we always have to focus on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One is the operational ability of the company to make sure that we continue to be able to produce water, almost at will.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And that has been compromised in the last few months with the inability by Hyflux or TPL to assure us that they can do so.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And that is connected with the second one somewhat, which has to do with the financial ability to support it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we will continue to work on these two issues because they are the most important ones.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They ensure that we continue to have plants that will continue to operate while under the PPP model.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The second question is whether we should bail out our investors.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The financial performance of companies, as mentioned by Minister Ong Ye Kung in a previous answer, depends on many factors.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It could include global business conditions, competition, performance of specific projects and also its own business decisions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, investors in search of returns must understand that returns come with some risks.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Before I answer specifically to that question the Member has asked, let me reiterate what I have said in my answer.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, while it is a current valuation and after the formalities are done, we are certain it will continue to be negative.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Like I mentioned just now, it is actually a positive impact on TPL.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Even if there are any proceeds from the takeover of the Tuas plant, we must remember there is an order of who gets what first.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: To that end, I have a few questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My final question is: how often has this situation developed in the TSDP?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Was it just in early 2017 or was it an ongoing occurrence?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB conducts many, many tests on our water system to ensure water safety, including TSDP.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we are certain that water supplied to our consumers is safe to drink and for use.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Even during the times when we had concerns about their operations, they were able to address these concerns.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But more recently, because of the financial situation, it begs the question whether that is sustainable.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we have put in the default notice to them to say that we are concerned: one, that operationally they are not able to address the issues to assure us they can continue to produce water; and secondly, that they are financially distressed and that they have not proven that they can sustain the plant for the next six months.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: How many times has this happened in the past?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Did it just occur in early 2017 or was it ongoing?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One is to assert our rights, stress Hyflux even further by asserting that right, and after the whole process, we may not get anything at the end of the process.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we have made the decision that because we are not likely to get anything from claiming the compensation, we have decided to not claim for the compensation.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We do have a lot of other big projects that are under the PPP model and we do have critical assets, such as power plants, that are operated privately.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: In that sense, how do you monitor all these assets and make sure that they are financially okay?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I was just wondering whether something could have been done in hindsight for this Hyflux case, rather than to wait until this stage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Well, as with any DBOO plants, PUB monitors the desalination plant – in this case TSDP – to ensure that it is operating reliably and executing its contractual obligations to PUB.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And then when troubles emerge, the responsible and fair thing to do is for PUB to require TPL to rectify it, and not to immediately issue a default notice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, to give them time to do so.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When these things happen – it is not just in the case of TSDP, it happens in other plants, too – there is a need to give them time to rectify.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If they can rectify them well and to the satisfaction of PUB, then the contract has not been violated.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has been in talks with TPL regarding its defaults all this while and has given TPL as much time as possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our duty is to ensure water security and take all the necessary steps within its contractual rights, primarily to protect Singapore's water security.
